executionPlan: Read constitution, QA insights, stage contract, reports 11, 12, 13. Ran lint, test, build myself on Node 22 with explicit exit codes (build in a rsync copy with node_modules symlinked). Scripted diff-scope, em dash and machine-path scan. Red check: copied tree, swapped in the pre-fix land.glb and fall.glb kept by the game-dev stage, ran the stance tests. Re-ran the bake twice from the original taken from git (a891bc4) and compared bytes, then did my own glTF-Transform inventory comparison and a collar-height check of moved neck vertices. Browser: headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol (software GL) against the running dev server, held keys through Input.dispatchKeyEvent, state sampled on the page side on every rendered frame (foot and toe joint heights, camera position, camera-inside-block test against the test arena blocks, plus my own added head-to-camera line-of-sight test against every block, with a canvas capture of the offending frame). Drops: 4 m end drops and about 2 m side drops, walk and run, camera yaws 0, 90, 135, 270. Camera drag probes at 4 spots near the wall and ramps (8 yaws of 45 degrees each, fresh page per spot) plus a pitch sweep. Regression and hero via the earlier round scripts. Playwright MCP was not used (it only taps keys). Several harness runs failed to enter the game under heavy machine load (load average about 300); those were detected (avatar at origin, hero camera) and discarded or retried, and are not counted anywhere below.
summary: REJECTED, one criterion fails (criterion 4, F6). Gates are green (lint 0, 145 tests, build 0 with / at 125 kB), diff scope is clean, F1 hard landing is fixed (feet at 0.022 to 0.027 m for the whole land state, natural superhero crouch from side, behind and three-quarter views, new stance tests fail 6 of 16 on the pre-fix clips), the bake is byte-identical and equal to public/avatar.glb with no visible shirt dots, hero and Play/Exit cycles are clean. F6 is only half fixed: the camera is never inside a ramp or wall block on any frame of any valid drop or 8-yaw drag, but (a) on 4 to 13 rendered frames of a run-sideways drop off ramp-30 the avatar's head and torso are hidden behind the ramp-45 slab edge with the camera on the far side, 1 frame at the end drop, and (b) dragging the camera pitch to its lower limit puts the camera 3 cm below the ground surface for 17 of 45 frames even in the open field, so the floor disappears. Also noted: foot height peaks at 0.051 to 0.056 m on the one or two stand-up blend-out frames (1 to 6 mm over the 0.05 m figure), accepted as a nit.

criteria.criterion: F1 is confirmed fixed in the browser: after drops of about 1.6 m and 4 m at walk and run, both feet stay within 0.05 m of the ground during the land state, the crouch looks natural from side, behind and three-quarter front, the fall pose looks natural while airborne, and the blends into and out of land show no pop; the new stance tests fail on the pre-fix land.glb and fall.glb in a temp copy.
criteria.evidence: Per-render-frame samples: feet 0.022 to 0.027 m for the whole land state after 3.7 m walk and run, 3.0 m walk, 1.55 m run drops (hips 0.47 to 1.01 m, smooth chain fall, fall+land, land, idle+land, idle). Caveat: on the final 1 to 3 stand-up blend-out frames (idle+land) the left foot reads 0.049 to 0.056 m, 1 to 6 mm over the 0.05 figure; this is the documented stand-up heel lift, no float or pop, so recorded as a nit (finding F9). The walk case of exactly 1.6 m was not hit (walk side drop left the ramp at about 1.0 m and landed hard from there); 1.0 m walk, 1.55 m run, 3.0 and 3.7 m walk, 3.7 m run were measured. Screenshots sheet-hardland-side, sheet-hardland-behind, sheet-hardland-front34 show a grounded one-knee crouch with a hand on the floor, and sheet-fall shows a natural fall tuck. Red check: pre-fix clips fail 6 of 16 stance tests (exit 1), shipped clips pass 16 of 16.

criteria.criterion: F6 is confirmed fixed: during the end and side drops off the 30 degree ramp, and while dragging the camera to at least four yaws near walls and ramps, the camera is never inside or behind a level block on any rendered frame and returns to full distance after walking clear.
criteria.evidence: Inside: 0 frames in every valid drop run and in 8-yaw drags at 4 spots (min clearance 0.20 m), so the round 2 camera-in-slab defect is fixed. Behind: my head-to-camera line test finds the avatar's head and torso hidden behind a slab with the camera on the far side on 13 and 4 rendered frames in two run-sideways drops off ramp-30 at default yaw (ramp-45 slab edge, screenshots occ-s20r-y0-0 and occ-s20r-y0-2) and on 1 frame at the 4 m walk end drop (head peeking over the ramp-30 slab, screenshot occ-e4w-y0-0). A fresh fall-behind capture over the ramp end also shows only the slab in frame (fall-behind-0). Separately, dragging pitch to the lower limit puts the camera at y -0.03, 3 cm below the ground surface, on 17 of 45 frames in open field (ground blocks have blocksCamera false); the floor top face is culled and the avatar stands on a void (screenshot occ-drag-open). Full-distance return: after the walk-clear the camera-to-pivot distance matches the free-field baseline (4.29 m both) so that part passes.

criteria.criterion: Every finding is reported with file, line, severity, trigger, consequence, evidence and rule, and the verdict is approved only if every criterion above passed.
criteria.evidence: Findings F7, F8, F9 below carry all seven fields. The verdict is rejected because criterion 4 failed.

findings.line: followCamera.ts pullIn 76-90 (cast from the lagging pivot, not the avatar); cameraProbe.ts 26-46 (castShape with stopAtPenetration false)
findings.trigger: Run (or walk) sideways off ramp-30 at default camera yaw, from 2 m or higher, and land beside or under ramp-45; or walk off the ramp-30 end from 4 m at default yaw.
findings.consequence: The camera is not inside geometry but sits across a slab from the avatar, so the avatar's head and torso are hidden behind the slab edge for 4 to 13 rendered frames of the hard-landing crouch (1 frame at the end drop). The sphere cast starts at the pivot, which lags the avatar during a drop, and a cast that starts overlapping a slab is deliberately ignored, so the camera keeps full distance on the wrong side. This is the very frame range the user judges for the hard landing.
findings.evidence: occRows from the page sampler: ramp-45, head (-7.7,0.7,6.5), camera (-9.04,2.7,2.15), camera clearance 1.77 to 1.86 m; e4 walk: ramp-30 1 frame head (-11.94,3.36,10.41) camera (-12.47,5.39,5.63). Screenshots occ-s20r-y0-0, occ-s20r-y0-2, occ-e4w-y0-0 (canvas captured on the offending rendered frame). Other yaws (90, 135, 270) and the run end drop: 0 frames. Fix direction (not made by QA): also test the line from the avatar head or chest (not only the lagged pivot) to the wanted camera position and pull in on a hit, or start the cast at the avatar position when the pivot lags by more than the probe radius, then add a followCamera test with an occluding slab between avatar and camera.
findings.rule: Stage criterion 4 (camera never inside or behind a level block on any rendered frame); code-review checklist: behaviour must match the criterion

findings.line: followCamera.ts 98-105 (pitch clamp pitchMinDeg -20 in config.ts line 60); layout.ts 69-72 (ground blocks blocksCamera false)
findings.trigger: Drag the camera up so the pitch reaches its lower limit while standing anywhere, including open ground far from any wall.
findings.consequence: The camera ends 3 cm below the ground surface (y -0.03, inside ground-a) for as long as the pitch is held, so the floor top face is back-face culled and the avatar appears to stand on a void with the level seen from underground. Not reached by yaw-only drags (0 frames).
findings.evidence: Open-field pitch sweep: camera y range -0.03 to 4.96, inside the ground block on 17 of 45 sampled frames; wall-north 16 of 48. Screenshot occ-drag-open. Fix direction: clamp camera y to at least ground height plus the probe radius, or include the ground in the camera blocker group.
findings.rule: Stage criterion 4 (camera never inside a level block on any rendered frame)

screenshotLocation: Session scratchpad, in the qa folder under a subfolder named m1-r3, inside its out subfolder. Harness scripts, logs and the red-check copy are in the same m1-r3 folder.
assumptions: Behind a level block was read as a block lying between the camera and the avatar (view obstructed), which is what the line-of-sight probe measures; if the user intends only the camera position itself, F7 drops to minor and criterion 4 would then rest on F8 alone.
Level blocks for the probes are the test arena blocks from layout.ts, regenerated by me and identical to the game-dev stage's list.

The exact 1.6 m walk drop was not reproduced by the harness (it left the ramp at about 1.0 m); the 1.55 m run drop and 1.0 m, 3.0 m, 3.7 m walk and run drops were used instead, all with identical foot behaviour.
Harness runs that failed to enter the game under machine load were excluded; none of the reported numbers come from them.
decisionsProposed: Camera pull-in should be validated against avatar visibility, not only camera position: cast from the avatar (or add a head-to-camera line test) and clamp camera y above the ground, and add stance-style tests for both.
lessonsProposed: A camera-inside-block probe alone passes while the avatar is hidden behind a slab; add a head-to-camera line-of-sight probe with a canvas capture on the offending frame so the evidence is the frame itself.
Harness scripts that spawn Chrome must close it on boot failure; failed boots left stale headless Chrome processes that raised load and caused further boot flakes.
Pitch persists across camera drag probes in one page, so per-spot yaw checks must use a fresh page or reset pitch, otherwise later spots inherit the pitch extreme.
